skill.name: godot-gdscript-patterns
skill.description: Master Godot 4 GDScript patterns including signals, scenes, state machines, and optimization. Use when building Godot games, implementing game systems, or learning GDScript best practices.
skill.summary: Use proven Godot 4 GDScript patterns for scenes, signals, gameplay systems, saves, and performance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown paths or normal Godot API usage in documentation examples. One confirmed issue remains: the save system example uses a hardcoded encryption key placeholder that could be copied into production code.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded save encryption key in the save system example.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the placeholder with guidance for project-specific key management, and label the sample as non-production until changed.

static_findings.snippet: # Create runtime copy to avoid modifying the resource

finding_verdicts.reason: ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request(path) is a Godot engine API for loading local project resources asynchronously. The surrounding scene management sample does not perform HTTP requests or contact external hosts.
The save system example defines a hardcoded encryption key placeholder. Although it is documentation, users could copy the pattern and ship a predictable secret.
The line is a comment about duplicating a Godot Resource at runtime. It does not enumerate the host system or collect environment details.
str(get_path()) records a Godot node path as a save identifier inside game state. This is normal scene-tree metadata, not host system reconnaissance.
The line is a performance tip about avoiding allocations in hot paths. It contains no system inspection behavior.
The line recommends signals for decoupling in Godot projects. It is architecture guidance and does not request system information.
The line recommends object pooling to avoid garbage collection hitches. It is performance guidance, not reconnaissance.
The backticks format a Markdown file path reference. There is no Ruby code, shell execution, or command invocation.
The backticks format a Markdown file path in the resources list. The skill is instructing the model to open documentation, not execute a shell command.

content.value_statement: Godot projects can become hard to maintain when scenes, signals, saves, and gameplay logic grow together. This skill provides practical GDScript patterns for cleaner game architecture and performance.
actual_capabilities: Explains Godot nodes, scenes, resources, signals, and groups.
Provides state machine structure for player and gameplay behavior.
Shows autoload managers and global signal bus patterns.
Covers resource-based data with runtime copies for mutable stats.
Outlines object pooling, component systems, scene loading, and save systems.
Summarizes performance tips and architecture best practices.
limitations: It is documentation guidance, not a runnable Godot plugin.
Examples target Godot 4 and may need changes for older versions.
Project-specific input maps, assets, and scene trees must be adapted.
It does not generate art, audio, or engine project files.

use_cases.title: Plan Gameplay Architecture
use_cases.description: Design maintainable scene, signal, and state patterns before building a Godot prototype.

use_cases.title: Refactor Player Systems
use_cases.description: Break movement, combat, health, and save logic into clearer GDScript patterns.

use_cases.title: Teach Godot Best Practices
use_cases.description: Use concrete examples to explain resources, autoloads, pooling, and performance tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a new game system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use godot-gdscript-patterns to recommend a Godot 4 pattern for my system: [describe system]. Explain the scene structure and signal flow.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Scene Communication
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate project with tightly coupled nodes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use godot-gdscript-patterns to refactor these Godot node interactions: [describe current nodes]. Suggest signals, groups, or autoloads.

prompt_templates.title: Design Save Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate game needing save and load behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use godot-gdscript-patterns to design a save system for [game type]. Include saveable nodes, data ownership, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use godot-gdscript-patterns to review this Godot architecture: [summarize systems]. Identify performance risks, coupling risks, and safer patterns.

output_examples.input: I need an enemy AI pattern for patrol, chase, and attack.
output: A state machine with Patrol, Chase, Attack, and Stunned states.
Each state owns behavior and emits transitions through the state machine.
The enemy scene keeps shared movement and combat references.

output_examples.input: My bullets cause frame drops when many enemies shoot.
output: Use an object pool for bullet instances.
Disable processing while bullets are inactive.
Return bullets to the pool after impact or lifetime expiry.

output_examples.input: I need a reusable health system for players and enemies.
output: Create a health component with damage, heal, and death signals.
Attach it to actors that need health.
Connect UI, audio, and game rules through signals instead of direct references.

best_practices: Prefer signals for decoupled communication between scenes.
Cache node references and use static typing in hot code paths.
Use resources for reusable data and duplicate mutable runtime state.
anti_patterns: Do not put unrelated game logic into one global autoload.
Do not repeatedly search the scene tree inside frame loops.
Do not copy placeholder encryption keys into production save code.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete Godot project?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that you adapt inside an existing or new Godot project.

faq.question: Which Godot version does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Godot 4.x and GDScript patterns used in that version.

faq.question: Can it help with performance problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for pooling, cached references, static typing, and avoiding allocations in hot paths.

faq.question: Does it cover save systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes encrypted save files, saveable nodes, load handling, and save deletion flow.

faq.question: Is it only for advanced users?
faq.answer: No. It includes basic architecture concepts and more advanced patterns for larger projects.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
